author: reek
body: Proc 0 stays on the boot processor, and the machine is genuinely multi-core while it does.

author: reek
body: The evidence is the core stamp. Whichever core wins the claim for a process writes its own id into that process's proc-core field, so the field is the claiming core's signature. Slot 0's must still read 0 after a run in which every other core was demonstrably busy.

author: reek
body: The control was run rather than assumed, and its shape is worth writing down because it is not the shape anyone would predict. A compiler was built with __idle_dispatch's scan-wrap forced to slot 0 AND proc 0's affinity put back to -1 -- both are needed, because either one alone refuses an application processor on its own, which is itself the finding that the affinity field is now load-bearing rather than decorative. The guest built by that compiler runs for seven minutes without printing a line and without faulting, and had to be killed. It does not report PROC 0 MIGRATED; it never reports anything.

author: reek
body: That is the failure the guards' own prose predicts. An application processor that claims slot 0 resumes the booted program on the boot stack and strands it RUNNING on a core that is not its own, so the waits never return and the test is a runtime failure rather than a wrong answer. A shorter spin was tried first and passed cleanly on the broken build: proc 0 is READY only in the instant between a child's exit waking it and the boot processor picking it up again, so a guest that finishes inside a couple of scheduling ticks never opens the window at all. The window is a function of how long the run is, which is the second reason the spin is the length it is.

author: reek
body: It needs a `.smp` sidecar; on one core there is nothing to migrate to and the two counters are both zero by construction.

author: reek
body: The spin is smp-preempt's, digit for digit, and for smp-preempt's reason: a scheduling tick arrives every few tens of milliseconds, so a child that finishes inside one is never a candidate for preemption on any core and the second reading below comes back NO AP WAS PREEMPTED while everything underneath works. The first cut of this test used a tenth of this and did exactly that. A shorter spin does not make the test faster, it makes it a test of the clock.
